::: {#exr-no-rejection-prob}
#### Probability that no test rejects

Let $A_1, \ldots, A_m$ be independent events,
where $A_j$ is the event that the $j$th of $m$ tests rejects its true null hypothesis,
and each has probability $\Pr(A_j) = \siglevel$
(see [significance level](inference.qmd#def-significance-level)).
Find the probability that none of the tests rejects.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#sol-no-rejection-prob}

No test rejects exactly when every event $A_j$ fails to occur.
Write $A_j^c$ for the complement of $A_j$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Prf{\text{no test rejects}}
&= \Prf{A_1^c \cap A_2^c \cap \cdots \cap A_m^c}
&& \text{(no test rejects means every $A_j$ fails)}\\
&= \Pr(A_1^c) \Pr(A_2^c) \cdots \Pr(A_m^c)
&& \text{(the events are independent, so their complements are)}\\
&= \paren{1 - \Pr(A_1)} \paren{1 - \Pr(A_2)} \cdots \paren{1 - \Pr(A_m)}
&& \text{(complement rule, applied to each factor)}\\
&= \paren{1 - \siglevel} \paren{1 - \siglevel} \cdots \paren{1 - \siglevel}
&& \text{(each $\Pr(A_j) = \siglevel$)}\\
&= \paren{1 - \siglevel}^m
&& \text{(a product of $m$ equal factors)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#lem-no-rejection-prob}
#### Probability that no test rejects

Let $A_1, \ldots, A_m$ be independent events,
where $A_j$ is the event that the $j$th of $m$ tests rejects its true null hypothesis,
and each has probability $\Pr(A_j) = \siglevel$
(see [significance level](inference.qmd#def-significance-level)).
Then the probability that none of the tests rejects is

$$\Prf{\text{no test rejects}} = \paren{1 - \siglevel}^m.$$

:::

::: proof
This is the solution to @exr-no-rejection-prob, worked in @sol-no-rejection-prob.
:::
